claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr experiences oxidation-induced pesting.
A thin ALD-deposited Al2O3 coating will significantly improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature air exposure.
The Al2O3 coating will not degrade the alloy's inherent room-temperature mechanical properties.
The Al2O3 coating will not degrade the alloy's inherent high-temperature mechanical properties.
Applying the coating as a surface treatment leaves the bulk alloy composition unchanged.
Applying the coating leaves the bulk microstructure unchanged.
The treatment produces a continuous and adherent Al2O3 surface scale.
The continuous Al2O3 scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The ALD-deposited alumina forms a stable, dense oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
The alumina barrier slows oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Slower oxygen ingress reduces internal oxidation and pesting.
Preservation of the bulk microstructure preserves the alloy's mechanical properties.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated specimens will exhibit less or no pesting relative to untreated specimens.
After the specified exposure, coated specimens will retain room-temperature tensile ductility comparable to the original 8–16% performance.
After the specified exposure, coated specimens will retain 1000 °C yield strength comparable to the original 163–530 MPa performance at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes substantial oxidation, pesting, and degradation under an air exposure near 800 °C for 5 hours.
